subtitulo: Mechanical design of a 35:1 reducer with a hollow output shaft, for a production run of 6,000 units
resumen: Mechanical Design coursework: a 35:1 worm reducer with a hollow output shaft, with its drawings and the animated assembly.

parrafos: This is coursework for the Mechanical Design module of the master’s in Industrial Engineering (ETSEIB–UPC): the design of a 35:1 worm gear reducer with a hollow output shaft, for a production run of 6,000 units. It was individual work, submitted with the assembly drawing, the lower housing drawing and the output shaft drawing.

bloques.titulo: Input side: lower housing and worm
bloques.intro: Step-by-step assembly of the lower part: the worm shaft, its bearings, the sealing and the lubrication.

pasos.texto: The cast part that houses the worm shaft. Only the bearing seats, the mounting feet and the holes are machined.

It carries the single-start worm. The motor end is hollow, with a keyway. I designed the shoulders and seats that locate the bearings and the circlip, with the required tolerances, and added the thread for the bearing locknut and the thread and tool relief grooves.
The bearings, washer, nut and circlip are fitted on the shaft. The two angular-contact bearings are mounted in an X (face-to-face) arrangement. Then the shaft goes into the housing.
The cover closes the bearing side and sets the axial position with a shim. The cover’s O-ring prevents oil leaks.
At the lowest point there is a magnetic drain plug that catches metal particles. On the sides, two sight glasses show the oil level.
The flange allows a motor to be mounted. The seal goes into the flange first, then the O-ring, and finally the flange is centred and fixed to the housing.

bloques.titulo: Output side: upper housing and worm wheel
bloques.intro: Assembly of the upper part. The lower part is shown transparent.

pasos.texto: Also machined cast iron. It encloses the worm wheel and holds the output shaft.
The shaft that turns at output speed. It is hollow so that it can be fitted directly onto the shaft of the driven machine.
The bronze worm wheel is bolted to the hub, which connects it to the shaft.

The key, the hub with the wheel, the spacer, the two bearings and the KM locknut are fitted onto the shaft. Tightening the locknut also clamps the hub and wheel on the shaft through the spacer. The assembly then goes into the housing.
On each cover the seal is fitted first, then the O-ring. The covers are fixed one after the other, with a shim used to set the face-to-face bearings to a specified torque.
On top there is a filler plug with a breather, used to fill the oil and vent the gearbox.
The JC-001 gasket is placed on the upper housing. Then it is joined to the lower part and closed with four through bolts and their nuts.
Both housings are transparent so that you can see the worm driving the wheel and the hollow output shaft. The output shaft turns once for every 35 turns of the worm.

bloques.texto: Assembly drawing of the reducer with two sections, several views and the parts list.
Part drawing of the lower housing: sectional front view, end views and plan view. Functional dimensions are toleranced and machined surfaces carry roughness symbols.

anotaciones.texto: Tolerance +0.030 / 0 with Ra 0.8. It houses the outer rings of the input angular-contact pair.
Tolerance +0.030 / 0 with Ra 0.8, at the motor end. The outer ring stays free axially.
Dimension with a one-sided tolerance next to the 7207 pair seat.
Five Ra 0.8 roughness symbols mark the machined faces and seats. The rest of the part stays as-cast.
210 × 90 mm footprint with four Ø9 holes for the M8×160 through-bolts. Overall length 275 mm.

anotaciones.titulo: Ø86 patterns with M10 and M6
anotaciones.texto: Two threaded-hole patterns on an 86 mm reference diameter, one at each end, for the flange and the cover.
Threads for the two oil level sight glasses, opposite each other.
Thread for the drain plug, at the lowest point of the housing.

bloques.texto: Hollow C45E (+N) steel shaft, 174 mm long with a Ø105 collar. General tolerances follow ISO 2768-m and unspecified finishes follow ISO 1302.

anotaciones.texto: Tolerance +0.015 / +0.002. They are the inner-ring seats of the two 7214 BEP bearings, 70 mm bore.
Ø75 h6 (0 / −0.019) and Ø85 k6 (+0.025 / +0.003): seating diameters for the spacer and the wheel hub.
Tolerance 0 / −0.19, equal to the bore of the SKF 26238 seal (66.675 mm). One section on each side of the shaft.
Relief grooves in details B and G, with Ra 0.4. Details C and F are Ra 0.8.
0.50 × 45° chamfers and R0.50 radii on the shoulders, and 30° chamfers of 2 mm at the ends of the inner bore.
Two 14 mm keyways inside the hollow shaft, one with a P9 fit (−0.018 / −0.061) and one with D10 (+0.120 / +0.050), with dimensions 37 and 28.80 (+0.20 / 0).
Dimensions 22 (0 / −0.30) and 9 (0 / −0.20). It holds the ISO 773 14×9×36 key of the wheel hub.
Thread for the KMK 14 locknut and a Ø105 collar 9 ± 0.05 mm thick.
